decisions.reason: Uses the install log and the manifest to trace the failure to the fs-ext@2.1.1 node-gyp configure build install script, pulled in by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, and blames the missing Visual Studio/MSVC toolchain.
Explains that the static top-level flock import in lease.ts loads fs-ext even on Windows, so skipping scripts leaves no binding and turns the install failure into a boot failure.

Uses both excerpts to separate the Windows named-semaphore path (acquireLockHandleWin32) from POSIX flock. It concludes that fs-ext is dead code on Windows and only needs to load, while POSIX keeps real flock and Windows keeps the semaphore.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: a win32-only no-op install script, an entry that loads the binding lazily and exposes import-safe stubs on Windows while POSIX stays native, registration in pnpm-workspace.yaml, a build-allowlist note, and checks for install, module load, boot and POSIX regression. The stubs throw instead of warning and doing nothing, but they are never called on Windows.
Explicitly rules out Visual Studio and any upstream edits, and uses the repository-managed pnpm patch.
Makes up a non-existent card slug instead of citing DSH-0.1.3-A1-03.

caps.reason: The plan never installs Visual Studio.
The report rejects --ignore-scripts and also patches the entry so it loads.
The fix is a local pnpm patch; nothing upstream is edited.
The Windows semaphore and POSIX flock are both kept.
